items.followUp: State one function of the nucleus and one function of the mitochondrion.

rubric.why: Identifies the main role of ribosomes.
rubric.description: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.
rubric.how: Award for stating that ribosomes make or synthesize proteins.

rubric.why: Names the product made by ribosomes.
rubric.description: Ribosomes join amino acids to form proteins.
rubric.how: Award for identifying proteins as the product of ribosome activity.

modelAnswer: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis in the cell.
They join amino acids to form proteins.

items.followUp: Name the kingdom to which mushrooms belong and give one characteristic of this kingdom.

rubric.why: Assesses knowledge of the five-kingdom classification.
rubric.description: Names the five kingdoms of classification.
rubric.how: Award for correctly naming all five kingdoms.

rubric.why: Confirms that the complete set is given.
rubric.description: Lists the five kingdoms without omitting or replacing any.
rubric.how: Award when all five names are present.

modelAnswer: The five kingdoms are Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.

items.followUp: Write the scientific names of mango and human.

rubric.why: Assesses the scientific name of onion.
rubric.description: Onion is scientifically named Allium cepa.
rubric.how: Award for the correct binomial name.

rubric.why: Assesses the scientific name of starfish used in school classification examples.
rubric.how: Award for Asterias or the more specific name Asterias rubens.

items.followUp: What happens to a cell when it enters the G0 phase?

rubric.description: G0 is a phase in which a cell is not actively dividing.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the cell leaves the active cell cycle or stops dividing.

rubric.why: Adds the relevant cell-cycle context or state.
rubric.description: Cells enter G0 from G1 and may remain there as resting or differentiated cells.
rubric.how: Award for stating that G0 follows G1, or describing the cell as resting or differentiated.

modelAnswer: G0 is a resting phase in which a cell leaves the active cell cycle and does not divide.
A cell usually enters G0 from G1; it may remain there as a differentiated cell.

items.followUp: What is the function of spindle fibres during cell division?

rubric.why: Identifies the structure forming the mitotic spindle.
rubric.description: The mitotic spindle is a system of microtubule fibres formed during cell division.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the spindle as fibres or microtubules.

rubric.why: Explains the spindle's role in chromosome movement.
rubric.description: Spindle fibres attach to chromosomes and move them toward opposite poles.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the spindle moves or separates chromosomes toward opposite poles.

modelAnswer: The mitotic spindle is a system of microtubule fibres formed between the opposite poles of a dividing cell.
Its fibres attach to chromosomes and move them toward opposite poles.

items.followUp: Define cytokinesis and state when it occurs.

rubric.why: Describes the characteristic indentation in an animal cell.
rubric.description: A cleavage furrow is an inward indentation of the cell membrane.
rubric.how: Award for describing the membrane indentation or furrow.

rubric.why: States the role or outcome of the furrow.
rubric.description: The furrow deepens and divides the cytoplasm, separating the daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it divides the cytoplasm or separates the daughter cells.

modelAnswer: A cleavage furrow is an inward indentation of the cell membrane in an animal cell during cytokinesis.
It deepens and divides the cytoplasm, separating the two daughter cells.

items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for cellular respiration.

rubric.why: Assesses the reactants and product of photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Carbon dioxide and water are converted into glucose and oxygen.
rubric.how: Award for correctly identifying carbon dioxide and water as reactants and glucose as a product.

rubric.why: Assesses the photosynthesis equation and its conditions.
rubric.description: Gives the balanced equation with light and chlorophyll indicated above the arrow.
rubric.how: Award for the correct equation with light and chlorophyll as conditions.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.

items.followUp: What is photolysis of water, and what does it produce?

rubric.why: Distinguishes light reactions from reactions that do not require light.
rubric.description: Light reactions are the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award for stating that these reactions require or depend on light.

rubric.why: Assesses the location or main events of the light reactions.
rubric.description: They occur in the grana, where light energy is captured, ATP is formed, and water may be split to release oxygen.
rubric.how: Award for stating the grana location or identifying a correct event such as ATP formation or oxygen release from water.

modelAnswer: Light reactions are the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis and occur in the grana of chloroplasts.
Chlorophyll absorbs light energy, which is used to form ATP; splitting of water releases oxygen.
